title: The Night Shift Reset
subtitle: The 28-Day System for Eating, Caffeine and Light Timing for Nurses, EMTs, Warehouse and Overnight Desk Crews Who Are Wired at 8 a.m.
author: J. Arek Thorne
description_html:
You can't fix a night shift with willpower.

Nobody tells you what to actually do at 3 a.m. Not what to eat, not when to stop the coffee, not how to sleep through a Saturday morning your neighbours have filled with a lawnmower. The advice you get is generic: darken the room, drink water, go to bed at the same time. Same time as who? Your body doesn't own a clock that matches your roster.

The Night Shift Reset replaces guesswork with five numbers and one sequence you can run on 12-hour nights, a 4-on-4-off pattern, or a rota you didn't choose.

Inside:

  • The Descent / Hold / Reentry model — why your shift is three short problems with different solutions, and why advice that treats it as one problem fails
  • The 3-2-1-0 countdown — the last food, last caffeine, lights down and no-clock times, with the arithmetic that makes it stick
  • Caffeine as a scheduler, not a starter — a half-life table showing what a 02:00 dose is still doing to you at noon, and why "I can fall asleep fine after coffee" is not evidence
  • The anchor-meal rule — why your big meal belongs in hour one, plus menu templates for one microwave, no fridge at all, and an 8-minute break that may not come
  • The $0 bedroom rebuild — towel, foil, duvet and a fan: what beats a purchased blackout setup, and the earplugs almost everyone inserts wrong
  • The drive home — why you must never drive when you are drowsy, the coffee nap that buys 30 minutes and no more, and the 20-minute rule
  • The bridge day and the two-step pivot for days off, plus the exact written script for asking your rota manager for a safer pattern (and the fallback that gets you a yes on something)
  • 28 days, one rule per day, with a 2-minute log that ends with a system tuned to your body instead of a study you'll never read

Also free with the book: the Shift Reset Planner web app — enter your start time, get your nap, light, caffeine and sleep alarms, printed as a fridge card. No account, nothing uploaded.

Not in this book: supplements, sleep aids, medical claims, or anyone telling you to just go to bed earlier. This is educational, not medical advice — no diagnosis, no treatment, no dosing. Written by someone who has worked nights, not by a clinician; read the disclaimer in chapter 1 and take it seriously.

Start with one alarm tonight. The rest of the sequence arrives over four weeks.
